rem:feynman-qou-comparison:
Remark Feynman vs QOU: term-by-term atomic mass comparison. The Bethe–Weizsäcker semi-empirical mass formula (SEMF) requires five fitted coefficients. The Wedderburn formula (three-invariant mass formula) derives binding from the Hecke algebra trace with zero fitted parameters. The SEMF is not the only external benchmark: modern nuclear theory is organised as a sequence of effective field theories (chiral, pionless, halo/cluster), each an expansion around a different low-energy limit of QCD with its own range of validity in energy and in nucleon number [hammer2019].

Term dictionary

See Table 1.

The table pairs each SEMF term with a channel of the Wedderburn formula term by term. The Coulomb row is such a pairing, not a derivation: the determinant channel \Phi_2 is not shown to be a Coulomb pair term, and on two nucleon blocks no braid insertion or invariant pair coupling gives one at n = 6 (see the Coulomb-charge definition).

Comparison

See Table 2.

The \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{QOU}} column in Table 2 records an unregenerated evaluation at the auxiliary loop parameter z_{\mathrm{aux}} = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) (938.910 MeV for {}^{1}\mathrm{H} and 3734.624 MeV for {}^{4}\mathrm{He}, mean error 0.074\%), whereas evaluating \Phi_1 at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) yields 935.352 MeV for {}^{1}\mathrm{H} and 3740.383 MeV for {}^{4}\mathrm{He}, with mean error 0.183\% and maximum error 0.321\%.

Across Z = 1\text{--}20, the five-parameter SEMF achieves a mean error of 0.023\% using eight inputs and five fitted coefficients, while the Wedderburn formula at z = q^3/(q^2+1) achieves 0.183\% (about 7.9\times the SEMF mean error) using two inputs (q_0, m_e) and zero fitted parameters.

Sources of discrepancy

The error in the Wedderburn formula tracks the nuclear shell model:

  • Under-binding for Z = 3--10. The transfer matrix chain overestimates \Phi_1.
  • Over-binding for Z = 11--20. The \mathrm{nn}/\mathrm{pp} asymmetry grows faster than the physical asymmetry energy.
  • Sign flip near shell closures (A = 4, A = 20). The Hecke trace detects quantum coherence.

The near-zero volume at generator k encodes nuclear saturation.

Improving: the pion channel

Including the hook channel supplies missing shell structure.

prop:neutron-proton-mass-splitting:
Proposition Neutron--proton mass splitting from quark crossing change. Assume (\mathrm{H}_\alpha): a change of the quark-ordering traced volume \Phi is converted to energy by the nuclear binding scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G, as \alpha\,\lvert\Delta\Phi\rvert. Under (\mathrm{H}_\alpha), the model neutron--proton mass difference is

  \Delta m
  := \alpha \cdot
    \bigl\lvert
      \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) -
      \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d})
    \bigr\rvert
  \approx 1.054 \;\mathrm{MeV}

where \alpha = m_e \times 8G is the binding scale and \Phi is the quantum dilogarithm volume.

The volumes are the traced-volume closed forms evaluated at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) = 0.6126880371 at q_0, pairing each strand with every later strand. This gives \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) \approx -0.614886, \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) \approx -0.896395 and \lvert\Delta\Phi\rvert \approx 0.281509, so with \alpha = 3.7445 the model value is \Delta m \approx 1.0541 MeV.

Comparison with measurement. The CODATA splitting is m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 1.29333 MeV, so the model value is about 18.5\% below it. This comparison is the empirical claim of the block.

A second model value. The corpus has a second, independent route to the splitting. The T^3 weight split of the z = q^3/(q^2+1) trace on the \gamma\gamma nucleon gives Q_\beta = \lvert t_{\mathfrak n} - t_{\mathfrak p}\rvert \cdot E_0 \approx 0.3254 MeV, where E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)) (tower-summed) is the corpus's derived hadronic scale. The decay kinematics m_{\mathfrak n} - m_{\mathfrak p} = Q_\beta + m_e then give \Delta m \approx 0.8364 MeV, about 35.3\% below the measured value. That route uses E_0 in place of (\mathrm{H}_\alpha). It fixes the size, not the sign: on its own it does not make the neutron the heavier nucleon. The two values come from different constructions, and neither is selected by its residual.

That is a claim about this construction, and not an exclusion: nothing here shows a quark-ordering volume cannot carry the splitting.

Two-term charge-insertion probe (record, not a derivation). The following facts about the 3-strand weight spaces W_p = (2,1) and W_n = (1,2) are proved: the quark-charge operators Q_iQ_j break the intertwiner P(q) between the two nucleon weight spaces; \mathrm{tr}(e_{(2,1)} V^3) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6 on the Borromean word V^3 = (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3; and the closed forms of the adjacent-pair traces. These are statements about a charge insertion. Two features of how they were turned into masses are choices, not derivations:

  • The braid content comes only from omitting a pair. Summed over all three quark pairs, the charge insertion differs between W_n and W_p by -\tfrac13\,\mathrm{tr}(w) for every word w; that is static charge counting, with no braid dependence. The word-dependent "connected" term keeps the pairs 1–2 and 2–3 and drops 1–3. The Borromean word does not single out the adjacent pairs, since each of its three pairs crosses twice.
  • The scale is chosen. The figures were formed with m_e, with E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)) (a definition), or with \alpha_{\mathrm{bind}}, under four weightings (plain, K_n/K_p, K_p^3, q), and compared against the \mu–p tension, the Q_\beta residual and lattice benchmarks.

So the keV, ppm and ppb values recorded with these files describe selected combinations, are not predictions, and are not scored. The splitting still requires a quantity the framework does not yet derive.

Canonical quantum-trace weighting. On the three-strand tensor cube, the quantum trace \mathrm{Tr}(K^{\otimes 3}\,\cdot\,)/[2]_q^3 reproduces the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) and fixes the canonical weighting without free choice; the plain, K_n/K_p, K_p^3, and q weightings serve only as labelled comparisons. For the covariant insertion Q_{12}+Q_{23}+Q_{13} summed over all three pairs, the connected part vanishes on V^3, so the resulting two-term contribution to m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} is zero. Figures such as M_{\mathfrak{p}}^{\mathrm{QED,conn}} \approx +0.2201 keV, \Delta m^{\mathrm{QED,conn}} \approx -0.3317 keV, and a \mu–p tension of 8.06 ppb (0.37\sigma) arise only from the 1/3-normalised plain weighting restricted to adjacent pairs; they do not hold for the covariant quantum-trace form and do not resolve the \mu–p tension.
prf:neutron-proton-mass-splitting:
Proof Proof of neutron proton mass splitting. The proton possesses quark content \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}; the neutron possesses \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}. At the quark level, the crossing types evaluate as:

  • \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}: same-type \to \sigma (eigenvalue q).
  • \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}: same-type \to \sigma^{-1} (eigenvalue q^{-1}).
  • \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}: mixed \to \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma + \sigma^{-1}).

Replacing one \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u} crossing with one \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing shifts the quantum dilogarithm by \Delta\Phi = \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) - \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}).

The ground-state configurations are \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d} (proton) and \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} (neutron). Each \Phi is the traced volume, with each strand paired with every later strand, evaluated at the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) at q_0: \Phi_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx -0.614886 and \Phi_{\mathfrak{n}} \approx -0.896395. This yields |\Delta\Phi| \approx 0.281509.

At the quark level, a more negative \Phi implies greater confinement energy (rather than reduced binding, as occurs at the nuclear level). The \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing (\sigma^{-1}) generates more confinement than the \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u} crossing (\sigma). This excess makes the neutron heavier.

By (\mathrm{H}_\alpha), the splitting is

  \Delta m \approx 3.7445 \times 0.281509 \approx 1.0541 \;\mathrm{MeV}.

(\mathrm{H}_\alpha) is an assumption of this block; no derivation of it is on record. The corpus's derived hadronic scale E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)), applied linearly to the restricted trace of the \gamma\gamma nucleon, gives a different value.

\square

Comparison with measurement. The CODATA value is m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 1.2933 MeV, so the all-pairs model value at z = q^3/(q^2+1) sits about 18.5\% below measurement (pairing adjacent strands only at z = q^3/(q^2+1) gives a -2.87\% residual instead; the all-pairs pairing is the construction stated above).

rem:mass-formula-validation:
Remark Mass formula validation: source classification and isotope coverage. The atomic mass formula recombines CODATA nucleon masses and AME2020 binding energies tautologically.

The ruler: m_e as external scaling parameter

Converting dimensionless mass ratios into physical units requires one external input: m_e \approx 0.511 MeV. This fixes the absolute energy scale.

The hadronic scale is E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0 - 1)) \approx 4.186 MeV. This agrees with the calibrated scale E_0^{(\mathrm{cal})} \approx 4.155 MeV to 0.75\%. The neutron Q-value is a prediction: \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = |\Delta\mathrm{net}| \times E_0 \approx 0.788 MeV.

Genuine predictions of the aether parameter q

The derivation chain yields:

  • Mass ratios: m_\mu/m_e = 206.768 (definitional).
  • Q-values: mass differences predicting higher-order spectral components.
  • Half-life ratios: \log_q(ft) values.

What \Delta/M measures, and what it does not

The denominator in Table 5 is the atomic mass, which is not a quantity this framework predicts: absolute mass is m_e times a dimensionless ratio, and m_e fixes the MeV scale by fiat as CAL-1, so a MeV figure carries no content beyond the ratio. Normalising a residual by it therefore divides a binding-scale error by a nucleon-scale mass, and the ratio is small for that reason rather than because the prediction is close.

sec:mass-predictions-derivations-preambl: This section presents the explicit per-particle mass derivations underlying the validation tables: the q_0 dressed-quark mass ratios and the knot-theoretic prediction for the \tau-lepton mass m_\tau.
rem:dressed-quark-numerology-at-q0:
Remark Dressed-quark numerology at q_0. At q_0 \approx 1.10998, combining Aether-pure derivation of the dressed-quark mass splitting with the nucleon sum m_p + m_n = 2M_N yields:

  \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} \;\approx\; 307.40\,\text{MeV},
  \qquad
  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} \;\approx\; 308.67\,\text{MeV},
  \qquad
  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} \;\approx\; 1.271\,\text{MeV}.

The splitting comes from M_N and q_0 through the convention-D pair Skein mass formula. The mean is fixed by taking M_N as an input. The resulting m_n - m_p \approx 1.2917\,\text{MeV} sits at -0.128\% from the CODATA value 1.2933\,\text{MeV}. This is the comparison already recorded for the conjectured mass split, not an independent one.

The mean dressed mass

Under the pair Skein formula with crossing weights w_+ = q^3/(q^2+1) and w_- = q^{-1}/(q^2+1), the nucleon sum is

  m_p + m_n
  \;=\;
  (5w_+ + w_-)\,\mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;+\;
  (w_+ + 5w_-)\,\mu_{\mathfrak{d}}.

With equal dressings this is 6\kappa\,\bar\mu, where \kappa = w_+ + w_- = (q^4+1)/\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr) \approx 1.0163 at q_0. So the mean dressed mass is \bar\mu \approx M_N/(3\kappa) \approx 307.95\,\text{MeV}, below the naive M_N/3 \approx 312.97\,\text{MeV}. The unequal weights w_+ \neq w_- move the mean of the two values above to 308.04\,\text{MeV}.

Distance from the aether bound

Two-sided aether bound on the dressed-quark splitting gives an upper bound of \approx 3.875\,\text{MeV} and a sharper bound of a third of that, \approx 1.292\,\text{MeV}. The realised value 1.271\,\text{MeV} is 32.8\% of the upper bound. The ratio is exactly \tfrac13\,q(q^2+1)/(q^4+1).

Heavier flavors

The aether flavor-split derivation is specific to the nucleon doublet topology. Extensions to heavier flavors remain unconstrained.
rem:m-tau-knot-prediction:
Remark The m_\tau knot prediction and its falsification. The CAL-2 critique (Epistemic status of CAL-1, CAL-2, CAL-3 — what is genuinely derived vs what is pinned) identifies a structural pattern in the muon-mass identity. Does m_\tau/m_e admit an analogous reading m_\tau/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(K_\tau)/\hbar_q^{k_\tau}?

Refuted over the searched census (scope-limited). A direct search evaluated 25 hyperbolic knots; no candidate matches within 1\% of the CODATA value 3477.23. The census-reach computation quantifies what the identity demands at the canonical q_0: for k_\tau = 3 the target volume \approx 3.382 lies inside the searched low-crossing range (between \mathrm{Vol}(6_1) \approx 3.164 and \mathrm{Vol}(6_2) \approx 4.401), so that exponent is genuinely refuted at the stated tolerance; for the CAL-2-analogous exponent k_\tau = 2 the target is \approx 34.14 — beyond any knot a 25-entry low-crossing census can contain (volumes near 34 require roughly fifteen or more crossings, links, or composites) — so the k_\tau = 2 identity is untested by the search, not refuted; for k_\tau = 1 the target \approx 344.5 is structurally out of range of any tabulated prime knot. This is retained as a falsifiable observation, without proposing a new calibration.

prf:terminal-resolution:
Proof Proof of the pair Skein nucleon identities. Write w_+ = q^3/(q^2+1) and w_- = q^{-1}/(q^2+1) for the two crossing weights of the pair Skein mass formula, so that \mathcal{S}_{ab} = w_+\mu_a + w_-\mu_b and w_+ + w_- = \kappa. Substituting into the two nucleon sums gives

  m_p = (3w_+ + w_-)\,\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + 2w_-\,\mu_{\mathfrak{d}},
  \qquad
  m_n = 2w_+\,\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + (w_+ + 3w_-)\,\mu_{\mathfrak{d}}.

Part (i). The cross term 2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}} appears in both sums and cancels in the difference, leaving

  m_n - m_p = \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}} - \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}}
  = (w_+ + w_-)(\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}})
  = \kappa\,(\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}).

Part (ii). The coefficient matrix of the linear form above has determinant

  (3w_+ + w_-)(w_+ + 3w_-) - (2w_-)(2w_+) = 3(w_+ + w_-)^2 = 3\kappa^2 .

Under the hypotheses, \kappa = (q^4+1)/\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr) \neq 0 and 3 is invertible, so the determinant is invertible, and Cramer's rule gives the two-sided inverse

  \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} = \frac{(w_+ + 3w_-)\,m_p - 2w_-\,m_n}{3\kappa^2},
  \qquad
  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} = \frac{(3w_+ + w_-)\,m_n - 2w_+\,m_p}{3\kappa^2}.

Substituting these into the linear form returns (m_p, m_n), and substituting the linear form into these returns (\mu_{\mathfrak{u}}, \mu_{\mathfrak{d}}), so the map is a bijection. Both parts are identities in q; no value of q and no measured mass is used. \square

sec:beta-decay-observations-intro:
Across the nuclear chart, \beta-decay half-lives span more than twenty orders of magnitude, providing an exceptionally sensitive amplifier for any error in the q-deformed transition amplitude. In the complex-volume decomposition \mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} + i\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta, the reaction endpoint \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \operatorname{Im}\mathfrak{V} measures the bar-odd curvature defect between adjacent isobars.

T_{3,5} weak vertex

The weak force is mediated by T_{3,5}. The vertex form factor is the canonical Markov trace of the T_{3,5} braid word in H_3(q), the coupling of the rate formula (hadron half-life), and it has a closed form:

  \mathcal{W}(q) = \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}\bigl((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5\bigr)
  = \frac{q^2\,(q^{12} + q^{8} - 1)}{(q^2 + 1)^2},

  \mathcal{W}(q_0) \approx 1.1875 .

The trace is the Wedderburn sum over the two blocks of H_3(q) that the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Markov trace weights, \mathcal{W} = y_{(3)}\,q^{10} - y_{(2,1)} with y_{(3)} = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2 and y_{(2,1)} = q^2/(q^2+1)^2; the sign block carries weight zero. At q = 1 the value is \mathcal{W}(1) = 1/4, so the classical vanishing of the decay rate is carried by Q \to 0 and not by the vertex factor. The half-life tables above use the single-crossing approximation and do not consume \mathcal{W}.

conj:n-v-bring-action:
Conjecture S_5 action on H_n(q) at the electroweak slice. At the electroweak slice \Sigma_{\mathrm{EW}}, the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_{n_{\mathrm{EW}}}(R, q) carries a faithful action of S_5 that fixes the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M. The Markov-trace-residual rescaling factor equals |S_5| = 120.

Forcing of S_5 over other finite groups

Three constraints force the choice of S_5:

  1. Bring's-surface symmetry. The conformal automorphism group of the Bring curve is S_5.
  2. Quintic intersection. The relation \sum x_i = \sum x_i^2 = \sum x_i^3 = 0 is S_5-invariant.
  3. TQFT level. The Reshetikhin--Turaev TQFT at level k = 5 has a Hilbert-space dimension matching EW gauge content.

Constructions required

Three ingredients are required:

  1. Definition of the EW slice.
  2. Construction of the S_5-action on H_n(R, q).
  3. Proof that the residual rescales by |S_5|.

Without these, the closure N_v = 120 \cdot q_0^{90} is an empirical observation with a -0.58\% residual.

Empirical evidence

The closure N_v = 120 \cdot q_0^{90} matches the target N_{v,\mathrm{target}} = 1.4455 \times 10^6 to within -0.58\%. The status remains conjectural.
conj:n-v-tower-depth-ninety:

Origin of the value 90

The factorisation 90 = 5 \cdot 18 suggests:

  1. Bring level 5. The EW closure requires five Bring cycles.
  2. Sub-level depth 18. Each cycle traverses 18 = 2 \cdot 3^2 Hecke generations.

An alternative factorisation 90 = 6 \cdot 15 suggests six generations traversing 15 structural levels. Neither possesses a formal derivation.

Constructions required

Three components are required:

  1. Operational definition of brane-tower depth.
  2. Derivation of 90 from Bring combinatorics.
  3. Sub-leading correction proof.

Empirical evidence

The integer L=90 closure minimizes the residual.
conj:n-v-leading-order-derivation:
Conjecture Leading-order N_v = |S_5| \cdot q_0^{90} (= 120 \cdot q_0^{90}). The electroweak topological invariant N_v admits the leading-order closed form

  N_v \;=\; |S_5| \cdot q_0^{90}
        \;=\; 120 \cdot q_0^{90}.

The corresponding electroweak scale prediction is v = 244.79 \;\mathrm{GeV}, matching CODATA to -0.58\%.

Derivation sketch, conditional on the two conjectures in uses[]

Assume (i) the Markov-trace-residual rescaling factor is |S_5| = 120, which is the content of S_5 action on H_n(q) at the electroweak slice, and (ii) the depth is 90 generations, which is the content of Brane-tower depth from m_e to v equals 90. Combining these yields the bridge identity v/m_e = 40 \cdot q_0^{90}. Substituting into N_v = 3v/m_e gives N_v = 120 \cdot q_0^{90}.

The step from (i) and (ii) to the displayed form is arithmetic and holds as stated. Neither premise is established: both are conjectures this block declares in its own uses[], and the depth-90 input is tracked as open. The section is therefore a conditional derivation, not a proof, and carries no \square.

Sub-leading correction

The exact CODATA value implies N_v = 120 \cdot q_0^{90.0558}. The structural origin of this correction remains unresolved.

Comparison to other strategies

The parameterization is optimal among non-circular closed forms.

Two separate claims about the prefactor 120 should not be run together, because only one of them is a derivation. That it minimizes the residual is a statement about fit quality — selection against the measured value, and so not evidence for the framework under the repository's no-fitting discipline. That it derives from the geometric aether is the assertion of S_5 action on H_n(q) at the electroweak slice, which is open. The residual-minimisation does not establish the aether origin, and the aether origin is not what the residual measures.
